Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, including mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau political exposed persons, and all cross-strait official personnel. Screening must be completed before incorporation filing and updated at least semi-annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) National Industrial and Commercial Administrative Service Portal – Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval System (公司名稱及所營事業登記預查申請線上系統)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Traditional Chinese characters. An English company name may be separately registered as a foreign-language designation and must not conflict with existing trademarks or company names. Romanization, if required, must follow the Ministry of Interior standard transliteration. The Chinese name must not contravene public order, good morals, or restrictive naming rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 股份 (Shareholding-related sensitive forms requiring special approval)
國際 (International) where it implies governmental or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed company name, the applicant may submit a re-examination request to the MOEA Central Competent Authority within 30 days of receipt of the rejection notice. If the re-examination is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of the re-examination denial. The appeal must specify the legal basis, the proposed name, and the grounds for overturning the rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not accepted for a registered manufacturing entity under Taiwan law. The registered office must be a physical location in Taiwan capable of receiving legal process and official correspondence. Shared office space or co-working premises may be acceptable only if a dedicated desk area, mail receipt service, and verifiable physical access are provided and reflected in the lease agreement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk, estimated at 25% annual inspection probability for a registered manufacturing address under ISIC 3240; likelihood increases if the premises are shared, appear non-operational, or have inconsistent signage with the registered business scope.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, administered through the competent National Taxation Bureau; tax registration and electronic tax services are available through the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal and the National Taxation Bureau e-invoice platforms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Taiwan subsidiary must first complete company incorporation or branch registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, and obtain foreign-investment approval where applicable. The entity then files business tax registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing business. The authority issues an eight-digit Unified Business Number, which functions as the principal tax identification number and business tax identifier. Required materials generally include the incorporation or branch registration certificate, articles of incorporation, registered office evidence, responsible-person identification, foreign-investment approval documents, lease or premises documentation, business scope information, bank information where requested, and an authorized-agent power of attorney. A foreign company without a Taiwan establishment generally does not obtain a Taiwan business tax number solely because it has non-resident sales; registration may arise if it creates a Taiwan fixed place of business, appoints a qualifying local agent, or falls within a specific cross-border digital-services regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan has no United States-style check-the-box election and generally does not permit an incorporated company to elect transparent treatment for Taiwan tax purposes. A locally incorporated company is taxed as a separate legal entity. A foreign company may operate through a branch, which is taxed on Taiwan-source income attributable to the branch, or through a subsidiary, which is separately taxed on its income. Taiwan has no broad statutory hybrid-mismatch election that converts a limited liability company into a pass-through entity. Group taxation and consolidated-return treatment are generally unavailable except for narrowly defined statutory arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added Tax under the Business Tax Act, with a 5% general VAT system and a separate small-scale business tax regime for qualifying businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to business tax registration. A business must register before commencing taxable business activities in Taiwan. The NT$200,000 monthly-sales benchmark is generally relevant to classification under the small-scale business tax regime and is not a general exemption from registration. Exported goods and qualifying exported services are generally zero-rated rather than exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uniform invoices may be issued electronically through the Ministry of Finance e-invoice platform or an approved private service provider. Businesses must use approved invoice formats, maintain invoice and transaction records, and transmit required invoice data in accordance with applicable e-invoice rules. Taiwan generally does not operate a universal real-time pre-clearance model for every business invoice comparable to certain clearance jurisdictions; digital transmission, invoice validation, buyer notification, and platform reporting obligations apply according to taxpayer type and transaction category. Business-to-business transactions ordinarily require compliant uniform invoices and purchaser tax identification information. Point-of-sale systems and electronic records must be capable of audit production and prescribed data retention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating generally applies to goods exported from Taiwan, goods sold to export-related businesses where statutory conditions are satisfied, and services supplied to foreign customers and used outside Taiwan, subject to the Business Tax Act and implementing rules. The taxpayer must demonstrate the export or offshore-use condition, preserve customs and commercial records, issue compliant zero-rate uniform invoices or equivalent documentation, and retain evidence of consideration and transaction identity. Domestic services performed or consumed in Taiwan generally remain taxable even if the customer is non-resident. Input VAT refunds may be claimed for qualifying zero-rated transactions, subject to filing accuracy, documentary support, and tax-authority verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs export declaration or approved electronic export record showing the exporter, consignee, goods description, quantity, value, and export clearance
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs declaration
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier manifest, or other carrier evidence showing shipment from Taiwan to a foreign destination
Sales contract, purchase order, customer order, or equivalent evidence identifying the foreign purchaser and exported designer-toy products

Foreign-exchange receipt evidence, such as an inward remittance certificate, bank credit advice, or other authority-accepted proof of settlement, where required for the relevant zero-rated transaction

For exported services, service agreement, deliverables, customer location evidence, payment records, and documentation demonstrating that the service was supplied to and used by a foreign customer outside Taiwan
Zero-rate uniform invoice, accounting ledger, inventory movement records, and VAT return schedules reconciling the transaction to the claimed zero-rated revenue
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax authority may deny zero-rating, recharacterize the transaction as taxable domestic revenue, assess the unpaid 5% business tax, impose statutory late-payment interest and administrative penalties, and disallow or recover related input VAT refunds. Unsupported customs records, mismatched invoices, fictitious exports, false foreign-currency evidence, circular transactions, or services actually used in Taiwan may trigger retrospective assessment for the relevant audit period. Intentional tax evasion, false reporting, fraudulent invoicing, or fabricated export evidence may result in enhanced penalties and criminal prosecution under the Business Tax Act and other applicable laws. Records should generally be retained for the statutory tax-record period, with longer retention applied where litigation, investigation, customs review, or refund verification remains open.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China achieves full current-account convertibility, with trade-related FX settled freely upon documentary verification; capital-account transactions remain heavily controlled, including foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injections, shareholder loans, and profit repatriations. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) may remit distributable profits to its Taiwan parent only after completing annual audit, tax clearance, and SAFE registration, and must evidence the remittance with a board resolution, audit report, tax settlement certificate, and the FIEs capital-account information. The renminbi (CNY) is convertible for trade on the domestic FX market, but cross-border capital flows are subject to SAFE aggregate-quota and post-verification monitoring. Profit remittance is permitted via the bank after the annual independent audit is filed with the Foreign Exchange Bureau; funds may be converted to original investment currency or retained as RMB subject to the 'Foreign-Invested Enterprise' (FIE) operating status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: SAFE abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds as of 2012; exporters under trade foreign-exchange category A (the default for WFOEs in low-risk designer toy manufacturing) may retain 100% of export receipts in a current-account FX or RMB settlement account and voluntarily convert when needed. However, trade verification requires that physical export receipts be matched to customs declarations via the 'Trade in Goods' Electronic Port System within 90 days of customs clearance; deferred receipt beyond 90 days must be declared to SAFE. No mandatory conversion ratio applies, but receipts must be directed back to China within 12 months for normal open-account terms unless a legitimate exception (e.g., pre-payment or consignment) is registered. For incomplete documentation or high-risk trades, SAFE can require full or partial surrender to the designated bank pending investigation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury operation due to direct digital EMI licensing not available onshore; offshore EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, WorldFirst) may partner with Chinese licensed banks to act as collection/virtual account services for e-commerce export receipts, but cannot replace a domestic WFOE bank account. Such rails are feasible only as supplementary settlement channels for designer toy sales on Shopify, Stripe, and local Chinese POS, subject to the bank’s notification and SAFE registration for the cross-border e-commerce trade category (Paying-for-Closing on E-commerce). Strict restrictions exist on foreign EMI holding WFOE funds or providing lending/hedging directly in CNY; all FX conversion must occur through a domestic licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a new WFOE opening its first onshore corporate bank account, the legal representative must appear physically at the bank branch or, at minimum, a senior officer with a notarized power of attorney must present the original seal and commercial registration certificate. Remote video KYC is increasingly permitted for simple second accounts or for the operating RMB account only when the bank has already conducted physical site inspection; however, for the Capital FX Account, SAFE rules require face-to-face verification of the FIE’s corporate registration, the SAFE FDI Registration Certificate, and the legal representative’s ID documents. Taiwan-director entities must additionally provide a cross-strait document authorization attesting to the legal representative’s identity, and the physical bank visit can be satisfied by the local resident deputy general manager at an assigned branch only if the bank issues prior written acceptance and the board resolution expressly grants opening authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is a Taiwan resident individual or a Taiwan-parent holding company with mixed business lines in toys and media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured corporate chart showing fully transparent ownership (individual or Taiwan company) up to natural persons, notarized certificate of incumbency, audited parent financial statements, and a written explanation of lawful source of funds for the FDI capital injection. Include registered UBO lists, passport copies, and Taiwan MOEA corporate registration extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value payment flows from online designer-toy sales (POS/Stripe/Shopify) that resemble retail aggregation or marketplace money-laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payable documentation package containing marketplace service agreements, channel settlement statements, product SKU cost analysis, shipping/vendor logistics records, customs export declarations, and a transaction-level export-to-payment reconciliation performed by an independent Chinese CPA. Include the business's e-commerce platform registration and ICP/business license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital account funding from Taiwan parent with recurring monthly injections structured as 'shareholder loans' instead of formal equity investment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI registration certificate issued by SAFE, capital injection plan approved by the provincial branch, capital verification report by a licensed Chinese CPA (including proof of foreign currency conversion), original board resolution, and written shareholder loan agreement with arm’s-length interest and repayment schedule registered on the Foreign Exchange Business System. Present a clear dividend distribution and capital-structure policy to avoid misuse.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP royalty or brand licensing payments to Taiwan-parent for designer blind box character rights, creating circular or layered transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP license agreement filed with the State Administration for Market Regulation, tax withholding certificates on royalty payments, strong transfer-pricing documentation using a Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) analysis or cost-plus method, and evidence of beneficial ownership (e.g., trademark/design registrations in the Taiwan-parent’s name). Include independent IP valuation and business rationale write-up showing the arm's-length royalty rate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Taiwan parent injects registered share capital via an external FX wire to the WFOE's designated Capital FX Account at the onshore bank. The remitting bank must use purpose code '622011' (Direct Investment – Paid-up Capital) or equivalent China-specific code '2202' (Foreign Exchange Settlement of FDI). The Taiwan remitter must provide a clear narrative referencing the SAFE FDI registration number and the 'FDI Statistics Platform Business Registration Form' issued by the onshore bank. After the funds arrive, the WFOE’s bank verifies the CFA 'Capital Account Magnet' system record, completes foreign currency settlement into CNY via a 'Capital Account – RMB Settlement Deposit Account', and requires a CPA capital verification within 15 business days for filing with SAFE. For loans from Taiwan parent, the routing must use a separate 'Shareholder Loan' heading with a filled-in FX liability registration and the debt-to-equity ratio ceiling (typically 1:1 for non-financial FIEs); repayment must follow a pre-registered schedule and pass the bank's offshore-related transaction review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Regular trade settlements for raw material imports (plastic granules, paints, moving parts) use Swift MT103 over the onshore bank's cross-border fast payment rail, with the required trade background documents (invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading/AWB, and customs declaration) submitted to the bank within 30 days before or after remittance. For high-value molding-material purchases exceeding USD 200,000 per transaction, an irrevocable Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) is the preferred rail, with the WFOE as applicant instructing the bank to issue through a Taiwan or Asian beneficiary bank. Additional clearing rails include China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) for RMB-denominated trade with Taiwan counterparties under the Cross-Strait Currency Clearing Framework, and the SWIFT 'Trade+With electronic bank guarantee' service for order-based supplier financing. Account disbursements to China-based suppliers and logistics partners are executed via domestic RMB real-time gross settlement (HVPS), preserving a clean audit trail for SAFE's trade verification system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: SAFE-approved Bank FX Forward (Deliverable) – matching a documented current-account trade exposure (e.g., USD collections from designer toy overseas sales against CNY operating costs) with a maximum tenor of one year and real trade background at deal settlement.

Cross-Currency Swap (CNY/USD) – used for medium-term conversion of an FDI capital deposit into working-capital liquidity or to hedge a shareholder loan repayable in original currency, but only after bank-level counterparty credit approval and SAFE notification.

FX Option (CallorPut on USD/CNY) – purchased through a licensed onshore bank to hedge price volatility on confirmed export orders without delivery obligation, with the underlying transaction identified in the customer verification process and subject to post-trade monitoring by the bank's hedging desk.
Interest Rate Swap paired with FX Swap – for synchronising the FX and interest-rate exposure of the capital injection and trade loans, permitted only for real economic exposure documentation.

NDF (Non-Deliverable Forward) – not permissible onshore for this WFOE; onshore entities are prohibited from entering into CNY NDFs when they have legitimate trade deliverable exposure. Offshore NDF activity in Taiwan/Hong Kong is only allowed for hedging non-deliverable CNH exposure and requires separate approval from the enterprise’s board and group treasury; CNH deliverable forwards are handled at the HK-DMA or Taiwan RMB clearing bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment may trigger statutory surcharges, interest, and tax penalties; applicable amounts depend on the facts and tax deficiency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of each fiscal year, subject to applicable Company Act requirements and permitted extensions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or complete required corporate actions may result in director liability, challenges to resolutions, and administrative sanctions where statutory duties are breached.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or update required information may result in statutory fines and repeat fines until compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit requirements depend on company type, public-company status, paid-in capital, operating revenue, employee count, and applicable tax rules. Confirm the current thresholds and whether a tax-purpose audit applies with Taiwan counsel or a CPA; no threshold can be determined from the payload.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan generally accepted accounting principles and applicable Taiwan financial reporting regulations; public companies generally apply IFRS as endorsed in Taiwan.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For an entity subject to Taiwan's company transparency reporting rules, maintain and update responsible-person and major-shareholder information through the Ministry of Economic Affairs platform, including the required annual confirmation and timely change reporting. Confirm applicability, reportable ownership thresholds, and exemptions for the specific company.
